value.title: Team data model + registry + programming team as instance #1
value.description: Introduce a `Team` data type and a `loadTeam(config, teamId?)` resolver in a new src/teams/ module, with a built-in 'programming' team that reproduces today's behavior exactly. Add an optional `teams` record and `defaultTeam` field to BoberConfig (Zod). loadTeam(config) with no id returns the programming team whose providers deep-equal resolveRoleProviders(config), whose pipelineShape equals the resolved engine, and whose memoryNamespace maps to the current `.bober/memory/` path. Named teams are built from config entries (providers merged over resolved defaults). This sprint is purely additive resolution + schema: it does NOT yet namespace memory (Sprint 2) or change pipeline-shape selection at runtime (Sprint 3). Zero behavior change is a hard requirement.

successCriteria.description: The project builds successfully with zero TypeScript errors (npm run build).
TypeScript compilation produces zero type errors in strict mode (npm run typecheck).
All tests pass with zero failures, including new collocated tests for src/teams (npm run test).

A Team type and loadTeam(config, teamId?) exist in src/teams/. A unit test asserts loadTeam(config) (no id) returns id 'programming', providers deep-equal resolveRoleProviders(config), pipelineShape equals resolveEngineName(config) (or config.pipeline.engine default 'ts'), and memoryNamespace is the value that maps to the current .bober/memory/ path (e.g. '' or 'programming' sentinel).

BoberConfigSchema (src/config/schema.ts) parses an optional `teams` record (id -> { displayName?, memoryNamespace?, pipelineShape?, providers? (partial role->provider), roles?, guardrails? }) and an optional `defaultTeam` string. A unit test parses a config containing a `teams` entry + `defaultTeam` successfully, and a config WITHOUT either still parses (back-compat).

loadTeam(config, '<id>') for a declared team returns a Team built from that entry: providers from the entry merged over the resolved defaults (resolveRoleProviders), memoryNamespace and pipelineShape from the entry. A unit test verifies a partial provider override (e.g. generator -> deepseek) is applied while unspecified roles keep the resolved default.
loadTeam(config, 'does-not-exist') throws an Error whose message names the missing team id. Covered by a unit test asserting the throw and the id substring.
No @anthropic-ai/sdk or openai SDK import appears anywhere under src/teams (grep returns nothing); provider routing reuses resolveRoleProviders.

nonGoals: Do not namespace the memory store yet — that is Sprint 2 (loadTeam may carry memoryNamespace, but memory.ts is untouched this sprint)
Do not change runtime pipeline-shape selection — that is Sprint 3 (the Team carries pipelineShape, but selectPipelineEngine/runPipeline are untouched this sprint)
Do not add CLI --team flags or a second example team — that is Sprint 4
Do not change the behavior of resolveRoleProviders, selectPipelineEngine, runPipeline, or the memory store
Do not build a .bober/teams/*.json file registry (Option A only)
stopConditions: loadTeam(config) reproduces today's resolved providers + engine + memory path for the programming team, and a config-declared team resolves with its overrides
value.definitionOfDone: A new src/teams/ module exposes a Team type ({ id, displayName, memoryNamespace, providers: RoleProviderMap, pipelineShape: PipelineEngineName, roles: Role[], guardrails?: unknown }) and loadTeam(config, teamId?): Team. A built-in 'programming' team is registered in code and is the default when no id (or 'programming') is passed; it reproduces resolveRoleProviders(config), the resolved engine, and the current .bober/memory/ path. BoberConfig gains an optional `teams` record + `defaultTeam`, validated by the existing Zod schema, with both absent still valid. Unknown team ids throw a clear error. No existing behavior changes; build, typecheck, and all tests pass; no SDK types leak into src/teams.
assumptions: The memoryNamespace value for the programming/default team is a sentinel ('' or 'programming') that Sprint 2 will map to the existing .bober/memory/ path; this sprint only stores the value.
PipelineEngineName is the existing union from src/orchestrator/workflow/engine.ts ('ts'|'skill'|'workflow'); pipelineShape reuses it.
roles is descriptor metadata (name/displayName) for the 7 existing RoleName values; it does not drive execution in this sprint.
guardrails is a forward-compat optional field, unused and unenforced (medical is Phase 6).
outOfScope: Any change to existing public behavior
value.generatorNotes:
Create src/teams/ with small single-purpose files (principle: small modules, unicode box-header section comments), e.g. src/teams/types.ts (Team, Role) and src/teams/registry.ts (builtin programming team + loadTeam). Collocate *.test.ts.

Verified reuse signatures:
- resolveRoleProviders(config: BoberConfig): RoleProviderMap — src/config/role-providers.ts:97. RoleName union ('planner'|'researcher'|'curator'|'generator'|'evaluator'|'codeReview'|'chat') at :10; ALL_ROLES order at :38. RoleProviderMap = Record<RoleName,string> at :19.
- resolveEngineName(config): PipelineEngineName — src/orchestrator/workflow/selector.ts:22 (pure, returns the name without instantiating). PipelineEngineName/PipelineEngine — src/orchestrator/workflow/engine.ts. config.pipeline.engine defaults to 'ts' (createDefaultConfig in src/config/schema.ts).
- BoberConfigSchema — src/config/schema.ts (full config object ~line 361). Add at the end: teams: z.record(z.string(), TeamConfigSchema).optional(), defaultTeam: z.string().optional(). Define TeamConfigSchema with all-optional fields: displayName?, memoryNamespace? (z.string().regex to safe segment), pipelineShape? (reuse the engine enum), providers? (z.record over RoleName -> string, partial), roles? , guardrails? (z.unknown()). Keep createDefaultConfig emitting NO teams (back-compat).

loadTeam(config, teamId?):
- If teamId is undefined or 'programming' (or === config.defaultTeam when that points to the builtin): return the builtin programming team: { id:'programming', displayName:'Programming team', memoryNamespace:'' (sentinel for current path), providers: resolveRoleProviders(config), pipelineShape: resolveEngineName(config), roles: the 7 roles as descriptors, guardrails: undefined }.
- Else if config.teams?.[teamId] exists: build a Team from it. providers = { ...resolveRoleProviders(config), ...(entry.providers ?? {}) } so unspecified roles keep resolved defaults. memoryNamespace = entry.memoryNamespace ?? teamId. pipelineShape = entry.pipelineShape ?? resolveEngineName(config). roles = entry.roles ?? default descriptors. guardrails = entry.guardrails.
- Else: throw new Error(`Unknown team '${teamId}'. Declare it under config.teams or use the built-in 'programming' team.`).

Do NOT wire loadTeam into runPipeline/chat behavior this sprint beyond what is needed to keep things compiling — the goal is the data model + resolver + schema, fully unit-tested, with zero behavior change. If you add a thin call site, ensure the default path is exactly today's behavior.

Tests: construct a BoberConfig via createDefaultConfig (or a fixture) and assert loadTeam(config) deep-equals the expected programming team fields. For sc-1-6 declare a teams entry with providers:{generator:'deepseek'} and assert the merge. For sc-1-7 assert the throw. Use no network and no fs (pure functions).

value.title: Per-team memory namespacing of the lessons store
value.description: Thread an optional per-team namespace through the lessons memory store (src/state/memory.ts) and the retriever (src/orchestrator/memory/retrieve.ts), and update every caller to derive its namespace from the active team. The default/programming namespace resolves to the existing `.bober/memory/` path (no migration, pre-existing lessons stay visible); a named team's namespace resolves to `.bober/memory/<namespace>/`. After this sprint, two teams' lessons are fully isolated in both directions.

successCriteria.description: The project builds successfully with zero TypeScript errors (npm run build).
TypeScript compilation produces zero type errors in strict mode (npm run typecheck).
All tests pass with zero failures, including new collocated namespace tests and the existing memory tests (npm run test).

memory.ts path helpers and public functions (appendLesson, loadLessonIndex, loadLesson) accept an optional namespace; a named namespace resolves to .bober/memory/<namespace>/ and the default/empty namespace resolves to the existing .bober/memory/ path. A unit test asserts both resolved paths.

Isolation: a unit test appends a lesson under namespace 'teamA', then loadLessonIndex for 'teamA' returns it while loadLessonIndex for the default namespace does NOT; and a lesson appended under the default namespace is NOT returned for 'teamA'.

Back-compat: calling the memory functions with no namespace reads/writes the existing .bober/memory/ path; a unit test writing a fixture lesson into .bober/memory/ (no namespace) is still loaded by the no-namespace loadLessonIndex.
retrieveRelevantLessons accepts and honors the namespace, returning only that namespace's lessons. A unit test seeds two namespaces and asserts retrieval is scoped.

The `bober memory` CLI and the chat memory distill (buildMemoryDistill) derive the namespace from the active team (loadTeam), defaulting to the programming/current path. A unit test exercises the CLI/distill namespace resolution (e.g. default team -> current path).

nonGoals: Do not introduce the semantic_facts SQLite table — that is Phase 3 (only the .bober/memory/ lessons store is namespaced here)
Do not migrate existing lessons into a 'programming/' subdir — the default team keeps the current .bober/memory/ path
Do not change pipeline-shape selection — that is Sprint 3
Do not add CLI --team flags or the example team — that is Sprint 4
Do not add memory hygiene/decay or reconcile-on-write (Phase 3+)
stopConditions: Lessons are isolated per namespace in both directions and the default/programming path is unchanged with pre-existing lessons still visible
value.definitionOfDone: memory.ts and retrieve.ts accept an optional namespace; memoryDir(projectRoot, namespace?) returns .bober/memory/ for the default/empty namespace and .bober/memory/<namespace>/ otherwise. appendLesson, loadLessonIndex, loadLesson, and retrieveRelevantLessons thread the namespace. All callers (src/cli/commands/memory.ts, src/chat/chat-session.ts buildMemoryDistill, src/orchestrator/memory/distill.ts) derive the namespace from the active team via loadTeam, defaulting to programming (current path). Lessons are fully isolated across namespaces; the default path and pre-existing lessons are untouched. Build, typecheck, and all tests (new + existing memory tests) pass.
assumptions: The programming/default team's memoryNamespace sentinel (from Sprint 1) maps to the existing .bober/memory/ path with no subdir, so no migration is needed.
Namespace values are constrained to safe path segments (alphanumeric/underscore/hyphen) — already enforced by the Sprint 1 schema regex — preventing path traversal.
The INDEX.md file is per-namespace (.bober/memory/<ns>/INDEX.md), so each team has its own bounded index.

value.title: Team-aware pipeline-shape selection
value.description: Resolve the pipeline engine / encoded SOP from the active team's pipelineShape instead of solely from global config. The programming team continues to select exactly what selectPipelineEngine(config) selects today; a team declaring a different pipelineShape selects the corresponding engine. The existing eligibility and 'careful'-mode downgrade rules still apply. runPipeline resolves the active team and uses its shape; with no team specified it resolves to 'programming' and behaves identically to today.

successCriteria.description: The project builds successfully with zero TypeScript errors (npm run build).
TypeScript compilation produces zero type errors in strict mode (npm run typecheck).
All tests pass with zero failures, including new team-aware selection tests and the existing selector/eligibility/workflow-engine tests (npm run test).

For the programming team, the selected engine is identical to selectPipelineEngine(config) today. A unit test asserts the programming team with engine 'ts' selects a TsPipelineEngine (same instance type as the legacy path).

A team declaring a different pipelineShape selects the corresponding engine. A unit test builds a team with pipelineShape 'workflow' (eligible config) and asserts a WorkflowEngine is selected, and that an ineligible/'careful' config still downgrades to TS (eligibility rules preserved).

runPipeline resolves the active team (loadTeam) and uses its pipelineShape; called with no team it resolves to 'programming' and behaves as before. A unit/integration test (with a stubbed engine) asserts the team's shape drives engine selection and the no-team path is unchanged.

nonGoals: Do not implement a new pipeline engine or a medical SOP — only resolve the EXISTING engines ('ts'|'skill'|'workflow') from the team's shape
Do not change memory namespacing — that was Sprint 2
Do not add CLI --team flags or the example team — that is Sprint 4
Do not change eligibility or 'careful'-mode downgrade semantics
stopConditions: Programming team selects today's engine; a team declaring a different shape selects the corresponding engine with eligibility rules intact
value.definitionOfDone: A team-aware shape resolver selects the PipelineEngine from the active team's pipelineShape, reusing resolveEngineName/selectPipelineEngine semantics (eligibility + careful downgrade preserved). runPipeline resolves the active team via loadTeam and uses its shape; the no-team/programming path is byte-for-byte today's behavior. Build, typecheck, and all tests (new + existing selector/eligibility/workflow tests) pass.
assumptions: pipelineShape uses the existing PipelineEngineName union ('ts'|'skill'|'workflow'); 'skill' still falls through to TS as it does today.

Eligibility (isWorkflowEligible) and 'careful'-mode downgrade are evaluated against config as today; the team's shape only chooses the REQUESTED engine name, then the existing downgrade logic applies.
How the active team id reaches runPipeline (an opts field or config.defaultTeam) is a generator decision; the no-team default must be 'programming'.

value.title: Second team as data + CLI wiring + docs (the platform proof)
value.description: Prove the abstraction end-to-end: define a minimal NON-medical example team purely as data (a `teams` config entry, no new code path), wire team selection into `bober run` (--team <id>) and `bober chat` (team selection), and document how to add a team. Running the example team must route to its own memory namespace, pipeline shape, and provider routing; omitting the flag uses the programming team unchanged. This is the sprint that demonstrates 'adding a team is data, not code'.

successCriteria.description: The project builds successfully with zero TypeScript errors (npm run build).
TypeScript compilation produces zero type errors in strict mode (npm run typecheck).
All tests pass with zero failures, including new CLI/team-routing tests (npm run test).

A minimal example team is defined purely as a `teams` config entry (a fixture/config, no new code branch). A unit test asserts loadTeam(config, 'example') returns its declared memoryNamespace, pipelineShape, and merged providers.

`bober run --team <id>` is additive and threads the team id to runPipeline; existing `bober run` invocations without --team behave exactly as before (programming team). A unit test asserts the flag is parsed and propagated, and that its absence yields the programming default.

`bober chat` selects a team (positional arg or --team) and routes the session's memory distill + spawned runs to that team; omitting it uses programming. A unit test asserts the chat session resolves the named team and its namespace.

End-to-end routing: a lesson produced while the example team is active lands in the example team's .bober/memory/<namespace>/ (not the programming path). A unit/integration test asserts the lesson location by namespace.

Documentation explains 'adding a team is data, not code', including the `teams` config shape, the three axes (providers/memory namespace/pipeline shape), and the deferred file-registry path. A doc file (README section or a docs/ page) is added/updated.

nonGoals: Do not build the medical team or any guardrail enforcement (Phase 6)
Do not add a .bober/teams/*.json file registry (Option A only; mention as deferred in docs)
Do not introduce semantic_facts or memory hygiene (Phase 3)
Do not add a second PRODUCTION team — the example team is a minimal validation fixture
stopConditions: `bober run --team example` and `bober chat` with the example team route to its namespace + shape + providers; default (no flag) is the programming team unchanged; docs updated
value.definitionOfDone: A minimal non-medical example team exists purely as data. `bober run` gains an additive --team <id> flag threaded to runPipeline (default programming); `bober chat` selects a team (positional/--team) and routes its memory distill and spawned runs to that team. A lesson produced under the example team lands in its namespace. Documentation describes how to add a team (config shape, the three axes, deferred file-registry). Build, typecheck, and all tests pass; existing no-flag behavior is unchanged.
assumptions: The example team is a small, harmless fixture (e.g. a 'docs'/'research-only' team) used to validate the abstraction; it does not need a bespoke pipeline engine — reusing 'ts' with a distinct namespace and a provider override is sufficient proof.
Phase 1's `bober chat <team>` argument was accepted but ignored (label-only); this sprint makes it actually select the team.
--team on `bober run` mirrors the additive pattern used for --run-id in Phase 1 (src/cli/commands/run.ts): absent = today's behavior.
value.generatorNotes:
This sprint wires together S1-S3 and proves the claim; it should add almost no new abstraction — only CLI flags, an example team fixture, routing, and docs.

Verified touch points:

- src/cli/commands/chat.ts: resolveRoleProviders at :28 and the ChatSession construction. Accept a team (positional arg like `bober chat <team>` per Phase 1, or --team) and pass the active team's namespace/providers into ChatSession so buildMemoryDistill (Sprint 2) and RunSpawner route to that team. Default 'programming'.
- Example team: declare it as a `teams` entry. For tests use a config fixture; optionally add a commented example to docs. Do NOT hardcode it as a code branch — it must flow through loadTeam (the whole point).
- Docs: add a section (README.md and/or docs/) titled e.g. 'Teams: adding a team is data, not code' covering the `teams` config shape ({displayName, memoryNamespace, pipelineShape, providers}), the three differentiation axes (provider routing / memory namespace / pipeline shape), the built-in programming default, and the deferred .bober/teams/*.json file registry. Cross-reference the research doc Phase 4.

Keep --team strictly additive (mirror Phase 1's --run-id). Tests: assert flag parse + propagation with an injected/stubbed runPipeline; assert chat resolves the named team; assert a lesson written during an active example-team session lands under .bober/memory/<example-namespace>/. Use temp dirs, no network.
